summary: Depth-first rabbithole dossier for Service Account Roles; source-anchored research pack.

facts.text: [low] Atlas roles limit which operations a service account can authenticate with its access token. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md
[low] You can't use a service account or its access token to log into Atlas through the Atlas UI. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md
[low] The limit for Atlas service accounts per MongoDB Atlas organization is 200. (verified as of 2026-10-15) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md
[low] The limit for access list entries per MongoDB Atlas service account is 200. (verified as of 2026-10-15) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md

[low] MongoDB recommends using service accounts instead of API keys to authenticate to the Atlas Administration API because API keys are a legacy authentication method. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md

[high] The Service Account object includes a list of organization-level roles and a human-readable name that is modifiable and does not have to be unique. Sources: https://www.pulumi.com/registry/packages/mongodbatlas/api-docs/serviceaccount/, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/terraform-provider-mongodbatlas/master/docs/resources/service_account.md

[low] If a project-level service account has access to the organization or other projects, you must have the Organization Owner role to manage its lifecycle. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md

[medium] Service accounts only grant access to the Atlas Administration API, which does not include UI access or access to cluster data. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access.md

[low] Each service account belongs to exactly one organization, and you can grant it access to any number of projects within that organization. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md

[low] The Atlas Administration API accepts service account access tokens (OAuth 2.0) and API keys (HTTP Digest Authentication) as authentication methods. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md
[low] To create a service account or API keys for an organization, you must have Organization Owner access to that organization. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access.md

[low] To grant a service account access to a project, you must have Organization Owner access to the organization that owns the project. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access.md

[low] If you assign an organization service account to a project, the Project Owner can manage the service account, including rotating secrets and updating the IP access list. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access.md

[low] IP access lists apply only to programmatic API keys and service accounts, not to other access types like the Atlas CLI or delegated access through Atlas App Connections. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access.md
[low] You should create a service account with at least Organization Read Only or Project Read Only on specific projects. Sources: https://veryfront.com/docs/cloud/integrations/mongodb-atlas.md
[low] You can create and update service accounts within the project. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/user-roles.md

[low] Users with a specific role can edit their own role or create an API key or service account to raise their privileges to Project Owner. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/user-roles.md

[low] For resources where the service account or API keys used to authenticate are not members of the hosting organization, Atlas responds with a 401 status code. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md
[low] Service account access tokens can only be used from IPs on the service account's API access list. Sources: https://veryfront.com/docs/cloud/integrations/mongodb-atlas.md
[low] If your key has both the Organization Owner and Project Owner roles, it has full access. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/user-roles.md
[low] An example configuration sets roles to ["ORG_MEMBER"]. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/terraform-provider-mongodbatlas/master/docs/guides/migrate-pak-to-service-account.md

[low] An example configuration sets roles to ["GROUP_READ_ONLY", "GROUP_DATA_ACCESS_READ_ONLY"]. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/terraform-provider-mongodbatlas/master/docs/guides/migrate-pak-to-service-account.md
